The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B-D?$
worked_solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{4\pi }{5}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{4\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{(\frac{4\pi }{5})}=\frac{5}{4}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cotangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $3$ units down. Hence, $D=-3.$

Therefore, $B-D=(\frac{5}{4})-(-3)=\frac{5}{4}+3=\frac{17}{4}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{5x}{4})-3.
$$
